cards.explanation: The answer is eight years, friends. Acts 9:33 says Aeneas had been paralyzed and bedridden that long. I think that's a heavy stretch of time. Eight is the number to hold onto.
The answer is Jesus Christ, friends. Peter says, “Aeneas… Jesus Christ heals you!” Peter doesn't take the credit. He points straight at the One doing the healing.
The answer is "get up," friends. Peter says, “Get up and put away your mat.” After eight years of lying down, that's quite a command. And the text says Aeneas got up immediately.
The answer is False, friends. The text says, “Immediately Aeneas got up…” No waiting period is mentioned at all. After eight years in bed, he's on his feet at once.

The answer is that they turn to the Lord, friends. The text says all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord. The whole area saw Aeneas after he got up. It's hard to argue with what they saw: a man who'd been bedridden for eight years, and he got up.

The answer is works of kindness and charity, friends. Acts 9:36 says Dorcas, a disciple in Joppa, was always occupied with works of kindness and charity. Always. Not once in a while. I'd love that on my own handle.
The answer is False, friends. The text says her body was washed and placed in an upper room. A tomb outside the city never comes up. That upper room is where Peter goes later.

The answer is that they urge him to come to them without delay, friends. The disciples sent two men to urge Peter, “Come to us without delay.” They sent people to ask him in person. I think they wanted Peter there as fast as he could manage.

The answer is the tunics and clothing Dorcas made, friends. The widows were weeping and showing Peter the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them. That's a closet full of her kindness. They don't just tell Peter about her. They hold it up for him to see.
The answer is "prays," friends. After sending everyone out, Peter knelt down and prayed. It's the first thing he does in that quiet room. Then he turns toward her body and speaks.
The answer is True, friends. After he prays, Peter turns toward her body and says, “Tabitha, get up!” He speaks right to her. That's a bold thing to say in a quiet room.
The answer is that she sits up, friends. The text says she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up. First the eyes open, then she sits up. Before that, Peter had knelt down and prayed.
The answer is "widows," friends. Peter called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive. Those are the same widows who had been standing around weeping. Now they see her alive.

The answer is True, friends. The text says it became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord. The news spread and faith spread with it. That's a ripple that started in one upper room.

The answer is a tanner named Simon, friends. The text says Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon. A tanner is someone who works with animal hides. Peter is the guest here, and Simon is the host.
